To address this need, we present Lifelong Learning Explorer (L2Explorer), a cutting-edge Unity-based environment that allows for continuous, flexible experimentation in a 3D, immersive setting. L2Explorer is distinct from static evaluation frameworks, offering several key advantages, including the ability to incorporate real-world data, easy customization, and direct agent deployment on robotics platforms. To further demonstrate the benefits of this approach, we briefly outline two prototype task sequences using L2Explorer, and we argue for the method's broader applicability to diverse, real-world problems, along with proposing new, more representative problems that can be addressed through continual learning. To support the development of evaluation methods and algorithms for lifelong learning, we also propose new, more meaningful evaluation protocols, and we emphasize the importance of leveraging simulation platforms that provide greater flexibility, including L2Explorer.
